doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: What a first trumpet player does
summary: Young explains the lead trumpeter leads the section, which follows and blends, and the leading players of each section must think alike.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: So what would you tell somebody a first trumpet player does? What would you say your job is as first trumpet player?
What is the job of a first trumpet player?
Boy, I‘m having a hard time today. I heard better yesterday than I am today. I mean, for some reason I‘m missing the main words you‘re saying in there. You say what?
What is the job of the first trumpet player? What does a first trumpet player do in a jazz band, what‘s his job? Because you have a soloist…
You do play some solos, but the first trumpet player‘s job is to, is just to, that‘s a very good question, I mean, to put words to that, the first trumpet player‘s job…well, I
tell you it‘s not easy to be the first trumpet player, or the first alto player, or the first trombone player. To be the first, you lead the band, you see…

Yeah, and the guys got to follow you and if you and the first trombone player and the first alto player think alike in a band, they‘re the leaders of the section. And so if them guys think alike and play together, the band is going to come together. It‘s hard to answer that exactly, I mean, as far as I‘m concerned to put words to that, because it‘s not easy.

I think when you said you‘re the leader of that section, that you‘re the leader of that section, that‘s important, because you‘re the lead trumpet…the leading trumpet, you‘re the leader of that section.
Right, and everybody follows you, you set the pace, you set the example and everybody goes with you, is that correct? Is that the role of the first trumpet?

Yeah, they got to follow you, they have to follow you and play with you. That‘s getting back to some of the things I was talking about before. If you got men that don‘t play with you, or think what you playing is the lead and they won‘t play with you. See, that‘s what I was talking about before, about playing together and thinking about what that man is doing or if you playing the second or third or fourth trumpet, and you playing you got to blend with this man, and if you don't blend with this man and if you don't blend with him it ain‘t going to work.
